explanation:

Multiplying row 1 with column 3: $1(2) + (-1)(\alpha) + 1(3) = 0 \implies 5 - \alpha = 0 \implies \alpha = 5$.

question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, then $A^2 + xA + yI = 0$ for $(x, y) =$

question: Let $G = \left\{ \begin{bmatrix} x & x \\ x & x \end{bmatrix}, x \in \mathbb{R}^* \right\}$ be a group under matrix multiplication. The inverse of $\begin{bmatrix} 1/3 & 1/3 \\ 1/3 & 1/3 \end{bmatrix}$ in $G$ is
explanation:
For identity matrix $E = \begin{bmatrix} e & e \\ e & e \end{bmatrix}$, $A \cdot E = A \implies 2xe = x \implies e = 1/2$.
For inverse $A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} y & y \\ y & y \end{bmatrix}$, $A \cdot A^{-1} = E \implies 2xy = 1/2 \implies 2(1/3)y = 1/2 \implies y = 3/4$.
Thus, the inverse is $\begin{bmatrix} 3/4 & 3/4 \\ 3/4 & 3/4 \end{bmatrix}$.

question: If $\begin{vmatrix} 2a & x_1 & y_1 \\ 2b & x_2 & y_2 \\ 2c & x_3 & y_3 \end{vmatrix} = \frac{abc}{2} \neq 0$, then the area of the triangle whose vertices are $(x_1/a, y_1/a)$, $(x_2/b, y_2/b)$ and $(x_3/c, y_3/c)$ is
explanation:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} x_1/a & y_1/a & 1 \\ x_2/b & y_2/b & 1 \\ x_3/c & y_3/c & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \frac{1}{2abc} \begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & a \\ x_2 & y_2 & b \\ x_3 & y_3 & c \end{vmatrix}$$
Given $\begin{vmatrix} 2a & x_1 & y_1 \\ 2b & x_2 & y_2 \\ 2c & x_3 & y_3 \end{vmatrix} = \frac{abc}{2} \implies \begin{vmatrix} a & x_1 & y_1 \\ b & x_2 & y_2 \\ c & x_3 & y_3 \end{vmatrix} = \frac{abc}{4}$.
Thus, $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2abc} \cdot \frac{abc}{4} = \frac{1}{8}$.
